name: Viewarr
description: The server half of Viewarr: does the sports and guide work once for the whole house, puts each channel's best stream first, acts on reports from the TVs, so every TV is quicker and keeps working with the TVs off.
author: petebutty

fields.label: How it works with Viewarr
fields.help_text:
How it works with Viewarr: Viewarr works without this plugin, but then every TV does all the work itself. With it, Dispatcharr does that work once for the house, every 5 minutes, and leaves the answers in each person's own Dispatcharr storage; each TV just reads them.

What it does:
• Live now and Sports: which games are on, in the leagues and teams anyone follows, and which channel shows each (from Dispatcharr's guide, ESPN, the Sky schedule and UK football TV listings weeks ahead).
• Recordings for sport: "Record all <team>" or Record on a game that isn't in the guide yet is made as soon as the guide lists it, even with every TV off.
• Score alerts and live scores: kick-offs, goals and results, only for the teams each person switches alerts on for (off until they do, in Viewarr → Settings → Sports).
• Best stream first: each channel's best stream (FHD before HD before SD; streams that keep failing on the TVs drop down) is put first in Dispatcharr, so every app and TV starts on it.
• Just added: what arrived on each streaming service in the UK in the last fortnight (films, and new seasons of shows), once a day from JustWatch, for Viewarr's "<service> · Just added" rows.
• Reports from the TVs: wrong guide, guide times out, dead stream, wrong logo or name, reported from Viewarr and applied straight away; each change can be undone.
• Measuring streams at night: each stream's real picture size and codec, checked with ffprobe in a quiet window, one at a time, always leaving the provider a line for watching.
• Live timeshift: pause, rewind and fast-forward any live channel, from a buffer kept here while it's watched.
• TV guide (optional, off by default): Sky's own listings for your region, matched to your channels and added to Dispatcharr as a guide source.
• Channel logos (optional, off by default): fills in missing or broken channel logos from Sky (channels the TV guide matched); every change can be put back.
• Backups of an admin's Viewarr setup (Viewarr → Settings → Users & profiles → Backups).

Each of these can be switched off below (or from Viewarr → Settings → Plugins → Viewarr); it's then off for the whole house and Viewarr hides it. Nothing needs setting up in Viewarr: a TV finds the plugin by itself. If the plugin stops, the TVs go back to doing the work themselves.

fields.label: Live now
fields.help_text: Works out once for the house what's live in sport now and starting soon, for Viewarr's Live now. Off: switched off for the whole house, and Viewarr hides it.

fields.label: Live now: extra channel groups to search
fields.help_text: Where the plugin looks for live sport for Live now, for the whole house. It always searches groups whose names sound like sport (Sports, Football, Events, Box Office, EPL…) and Event Channel Managarr's groups if you use it. Add any others here, one per line or separated by commas, e.g. your provider's event-feed groups (UEFA, SOCCER, PDC). Use the names as Dispatcharr shows them. Easier: switch a group on in Viewarr → Settings → Live TV → Live now groups and the plugin searches it too (from the next round), so this box is only needed as a fallback. Each TV can also switch groups, sports and leagues off for itself there.

fields.label: Followed games and where they're on
fields.help_text: The fixtures of every team and league anyone follows (ESPN), and which channel shows each game, from Dispatcharr's guide, the Sky schedule and UK football TV listings weeks ahead, for Viewarr's Sports page. Off: nothing is fetched here; the Sports page places games from each TV's own guide only. Sport recordings and score alerts need this on.

fields.label: Sport recordings
fields.help_text: "Record all <team>" and Record on a game the guide doesn't list yet: the recording is made as soon as the guide lists it, even with every TV off. Needs "Followed games" on. Off: switched off for the whole house, and Viewarr hides it. (Recording a game that's already in the guide still works.)

fields.label: Score alerts and live scores
fields.help_text: Kick-offs, goals and results checked every 45 seconds while a followed game is on, for the alert banner and the ticker's Live scores (each person still chooses their teams in Viewarr → Settings → Sports). Needs "Followed games" on. Off: switched off for the whole house, and Viewarr hides it.

fields.label: Event channels: only with a listing
fields.help_text: Tells the TVs which channels are event channels (the plugin's event groups), so Viewarr can hide those with nothing listed now or in the next 24 hours (each person's Settings → Live TV → Event channels). Off: every event channel is always shown, and Viewarr hides the option.

fields.label: Just added (JustWatch)
fields.help_text: What arrived on each streaming service in the UK in the last fortnight, fetched once a day from JustWatch for Viewarr's "<service> · Just added" rows. Off: switched off for the whole house, and Viewarr hides it.

fields.label: IPTV progress sync (optional, without Trakt)
fields.help_text: Optional, for people who don't use Trakt. When someone switches on Viewarr → Settings → Playback → Watch progress → "Sync IPTV progress with my Emby / Jellyfin / Plex", this keeps what they watched on IPTV in step with their own server every 5 minutes, matched by TMDB id: finish a film on IPTV and it's ticked in Plex. It only touches titles they've played on IPTV; things only watched on the server stay there. Their server sign-in comes from Viewarr and is kept in their own Dispatcharr storage, not on this page. If you use Trakt, leave it off: Trakt already does this.

fields.label: IPTV progress sync (Plex, Jellyfin, Emby)
fields.help_text: The house-wide switch for keeping IPTV watch progress in step with each person's own Plex, Jellyfin or Emby (see above); each person still switches it on for themselves in Viewarr. Off: switched off for the whole house, and Viewarr hides it.

fields.label: Best stream first
fields.help_text: Puts each channel's best stream first in Dispatcharr, so every app and TV starts on it; streams that keep failing on the TVs drop down the list. Only channels with more than one stream, never Event Channel Managarr's groups; a channel is moved at most once an hour. "Put stream order back" below undoes every move.

fields.label: Act on reports from the TVs
fields.help_text: Reports sent from Viewarr (wrong guide, dead stream, wrong logo or name) are applied straight away; admins can undo each one from Viewarr or with the Undo action.

fields.label: Groups never reported
fields.help_text: Channel groups that are off air most of the time by nature (club TV; event groups are always included). Their streams are never marked as failing or measured, and dead-stream reports about them are logged only. Comma-separated.

fields.label: Change to undo (id)
fields.help_text: Only for the "Undo a change" button on this page: paste the id of a change from "Recent changes from reports" here, save, then press the button. Viewarr sends the id itself.

fields.label: Measure streams at night
fields.help_text: Checks each stream's picture size and codec with ffprobe while nobody is watching, a few seconds per stream, so the best-stream order uses real quality rather than names. Uses one provider connection at a time.

fields.label: Measuring window (local time)
fields.help_text: When measuring may run, as HH:MM-HH:MM in the server's local time, e.g. 01:00-07:00. Leave empty to never measure on a schedule (the "Measure streams now" button still works).

fields.label: Measure these channel groups first
fields.default: Entertainment, Movies, Sports, News, Kids, Music, UK Regional, Club TV
fields.help_text: Dispatcharr channel groups in the order to measure them, comma-separated; each group is finished before the next. Groups not listed follow alphabetically. Event Channel Managarr's groups are never measured.

fields.label: Measure only the listed groups
fields.help_text: On: channels in groups not listed above are skipped altogether.

fields.label: Provider to measure first
fields.help_text: The M3U account whose streams come first within each group, by name as Dispatcharr shows it. Empty: the provider with the most streams still to measure.

fields.label: Live timeshift (pause and rewind live TV)
fields.help_text: While a TV watches a channel, the last couple of hours of it are kept on this server, so Viewarr can pause, rewind and fast-forward any channel, not only ones with catch-up. One copy per channel, shared by every TV watching it, taken from Dispatcharr's own stream, so it uses no extra provider connection. It stops a minute after the last TV leaves the channel (at once when a TV changes channel) and the files are deleted. Each person can still switch it off for themselves in Viewarr → Settings → Live TV. Off: switched off for the whole house, and Viewarr hides it.

fields.label: Live timeshift: channels
fields.help_text: Only channels without catch-up: channels with the provider's catch-up keep using that for pause and rewind, saving disk space and a buffer each.

fields.label: Live timeshift: buffer length
fields.help_text: How far back a TV can rewind on a channel (from when the first TV started watching it). An HD channel takes about 3 GB an hour on the server while it's being watched.

fields.label: Live timeshift: channels at once
fields.help_text: At most this many channels are buffered at the same time; a TV on another channel then has catch-up (if the channel has it) or live TV only, as without the plugin.

fields.label: Live timeshift: where it's kept
fields.help_text: Always in /data/timeshift inside Dispatcharr's container, like Dispatcharr's own /data/recordings. Left alone, that's a folder in Dispatcharr's data folder. For a better place, map a fast disk to /data/timeshift in Docker: on Unraid, a cache-only share (Secondary storage: None) so the mover never touches it. Sports service status shows the free space.

fields.label: Backups
fields.help_text: Lets admins save and restore their Viewarr setup here (Viewarr → Settings → Users & profiles → Backups). Off: Viewarr hides Backups; the ones already saved are kept.

fields.label: TV guide (Sky)
fields.help_text: Optional, off by default. Twice a day (04:30 and 16:30) the plugin reads Sky's own listings for your region, matches your channels to Sky's by name, and writes a guide for the matched channels to /data/logos/viewarr-epg/guide.xml, added to Dispatcharr as the guide source "Viewarr: Sky guide". To begin with nothing else changes: compare it with your current guide ("Compare guide with another source" below), then switch on "Point matched channels at this guide". Channels it couldn't match, and its least sure matches, are listed by "TV guide status"; fix them with "TV guide: channel overrides".

fields.label: TV guide (Sky)
fields.help_text: Fetches Sky's listings for the matched channels twice a day (and straight away when switched on) and keeps the "Viewarr: Sky guide" source in Dispatcharr up to date. Off: nothing is fetched, and any channel pointed at this guide goes back to the guide it had before.

fields.label: TV guide: listings source
fields.help_text: Where the listings come from. Only Sky (UK) for now.

fields.label: TV guide: Sky region
fields.help_text: Your Sky region. The national channels are the same everywhere; the region decides BBC One, ITV / STV / UTV and the channel numbers (which help the matching).

fields.label: TV guide: days ahead
fields.help_text: How many days of listings to fetch (Sky has about 8).

fields.label: Point matched channels at this guide
fields.help_text: On: every matched channel is set to use the "Viewarr: Sky guide" in Dispatcharr. The guide each one had before is remembered and put back when this (or the TV guide) is switched off. Off (the default): nothing in your channels' guide mapping changes, so you can compare both guides side by side first.

fields.label: TV guide: channel overrides
fields.help_text: Fix a match by hand: "Dispatcharr channel name = Sky channel name", separated by ; or new lines, e.g. "Sky Cinema Hits = MockingjayHD; Nicktoons = Nick SpongeBob". Use the Sky name as "TV guide status" shows it, or its id (sky.4033). "Channel = -" never matches that channel.

fields.label: Channel logos from Sky
fields.help_text: Logos for channels the TV guide matched to Sky (needs the TV guide on). Only missing: channels with no logo, or a broken one. All: Sky's logo for every matched channel. Off puts back the logos it changed; a logo you change by hand is never touched.

actions.label: Sports service status
actions.description: When it last worked out Live now and the games, and how much.

actions.label: Refresh sports now
actions.description: Asks the sports service to work out Live now and the games straight away: the round starts within a minute (see "Sports service status").

actions.label: Preview stream order
actions.description: Shows which channels Best stream first would change right now, without changing anything.

actions.label: Put stream order back
actions.description: Every channel that Best stream first moved goes back to the order it had before the first move.

confirm.title: Put stream order back?
confirm.message: Every channel moved by Best stream first goes back to its original order. If the setting stays on, the next round may move them again. Continue?

actions.label: Undo a change
actions.description: Reverses one change made from a TV's report. Takes the change's id (parameter "id", or the "Change to undo" box above).

actions.label: Recent changes from reports
actions.description: The last 10 changes made from reports sent by the TVs, with their ids.

actions.label: Measure streams now
actions.description: One batch of up to 20 streams, ignoring the window: queued for the measuring thread, it starts within a minute and takes up to about 2½ minutes (the results show in the sports service status). A provider's spare line is still respected: nothing is probed while that would take the last line.

actions.label: TV guide status
actions.description: When the TV guide was last fetched, how many channels matched, the least sure matches, and the channels it couldn't match (with a likely Sky channel to use in the overrides).

actions.label: Fetch the TV guide now
actions.description: Queues a fetch of Sky's channel list and listings: it starts within a minute and takes about a minute; it rewrites the guide file and refreshes the "Viewarr: Sky guide" source.

actions.label: Compare guide with another source
actions.description: For every matched channel, the next 24 hours of the Sky guide against the guide the channel uses now (or used before it was pointed here): the share of programmes with the same title starting within 5 minutes. Optional parameter "source" limits it to channels on that guide source, e.g. Sky (iptv-org).

actions.label: Channel logos status
actions.description: How many channels use a logo from Sky, how many kept their own, and how many the plugin has changed (put back when switched off).

actions.label: Preview channel logos
actions.description: What "Channel logos from Sky" would change right now, without changing anything (optional parameters "mode" = missing / all and "sources" = sky_tvlogos / sky / tvlogos to try other settings). It only uses logo addresses already checked, so it answers quickly; ones not checked yet are counted as not judged until the next run checks them.
